phase: M6 Phase 5K - Prompt-Injection Architecture Decision + Targeted Security Fix
executive_summary: Phase 5J's remaining blocker was a narrow forced-fixed-output injection pattern (5/31 FULL cases). Forensically compared ingestion-side (Option A) vs output-side (Option B) defenses using only real evidence before writing code. Option A rejected: requires Team4A modification (out of bounds) AND a best-faith keyword detector showed 5/8 detection with 3/11 (27%) false positives on ordinary educational imperative language. Option B: first candidate design (zero-overlap heuristic) tested and found completely ineffective (0/9 true positives) because a successful attack's output is by definition drawn from the evidence. Revised design (short answer as exact contiguous quoted span within evidence) tested against 68 real live-captured answers: 8/8 true positives, 0/59 false positives. Classification A - implemented as an additive ~40-line function wired into LLMGenerator.generate(). Post-fix full regression: 0/32 FULL cases (down from 5/31), 1 PARTIAL unchanged (out of scope by design), zero new false positives, zero pytest regressions, zero Qdrant drift, Team4A/Team4C untouched.

attack_reproduction.methodological_finding: LLM generation is not perfectly deterministic run-to-run (3/5 reproduced as FULL failures, 2/5 resisted this run, same code/input). Root-cause finding remains valid and reproducible; single-run severity counts are a snapshot not a guaranteed-stable rate. Accounted for in evaluation methodology (answer-content-based ground truth, not case-ID-based).

trust_boundary_root_cause: Ollama called via /api/generate with the entire prompt collapsed into one flat string - no API-level role separation. Phase 5F's delimiter+neutralization defense is prompt-level: tells the model retrieved text is untrusted but cannot prevent semantic recognition/compliance with a short unambiguous imperative sentence embedded in that data. Fundamental limitation of prompt-level defenses against instruction-following models, not an implementation bug. This phase's fix does not touch this boundary; it adds an independent downstream check on the model's actual output.

option_a_ingestion_side.conclusion: even a generously-scoped deterministic pattern detector cannot reliably distinguish malicious instructions from ordinary imperative educational prose across languages/scripts without real language understanding, which is prohibited this phase without approval

v1_candidate.design: flag short answer (<=6 tokens) with zero token overlap with both query and evidence
v1_candidate.root_cause_of_failure: a successful attack's output is by definition drawn from the evidence (attacker's chosen string is written directly inside the malicious chunk), so 'no evidence overlap' is exactly the wrong signal

v2_candidate.design: flag short answer (<=6 tokens, script-agnostic ASCII+Devanagari tokenization matching bm25_index.py's own default_tokenizer pattern) that appears as an exact contiguous quoted span inside a single retrieved chunk's raw text; excludes the system's own INSUFFICIENT_CONTEXT_MESSAGE
v2_candidate.test_corpus: 68 real live-captured answers: Phase 5J 31-case main battery + 31-case injection battery + 5-case supplement + this phase's 5-case fresh repro; no new LLM calls needed
